title: Request-to-Contract Playbook: Access, Procurement, Vendor & Travel Guidance
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook documents a single, cohesive operational flow from an internal request (access, expense, travel, or procurement) through approval to execution and contract closeout. It is intended for managers, requestors, finance partners, security, and vendor teams. The goal is to reduce cycle time, centralize audit evidence, and ensure consistent risk controls for vendor onboarding and sensitive access.

Scope:
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and partners requesting:
  - System access and elevated permissions
  - Hardware or software procurement (including cloud credits and ML instance reservations)
  - Vendor engagements (SOWs, MSA, pilots)
  - Business travel and associated expense requests
- Excludes: petty cash reimbursements under $50 (see Finance petty-cash policy).

Key principles:
- Principle of least privilege for access requests.
- Segregation of duties across requestor, approver, and approver-within-security/finance for high-risk actions.
- Evidence-first procurement: every spend must have a request, approval, and an owner.
- Centralized vendor records and contract indexing for discoverability and audits.

How to use this playbook:
- Follow the numbered workflow for the request type.
- Use the included templates (Access Request, Procurement Request, Vendor Checklist, Travel Pre-Approval) and attach to the ticket.
- Escalate via the incident-channel if approvals exceed SLA windows.

1) Roles & Responsibilities (high level):
- Requestor: initiates request, provides justification, attaches attachments, and responds to clarifying questions.
- Line Manager / Budget Owner: confirms business need and approves budget.
- Finance Approver: verifies budget coding and cost center alignment.
- Security Reviewer: reviews access requests with sensitive scopes, approves vendor security posture for contracts.
- Procurement / Legal: reviews contract terms above threshold or non-standard terms.
- Vendor Owner: Redwood employee who will own the vendor relationship and renewal.

RACI at a glance (examples):
- Access request <= 30 days: Requestor (R), Manager (A), Security (C), IT Ops (I)
- Purchase order <= $10k: Requestor (R), Manager (A), Finance (C), Procurement (I)
- Contract > $50k or data-bearing vendor: Requestor (R), Manager (C), Finance (C), Legal (A), Security (A)

2) Access & Permissions Workflow:
Purpose: Provide a fast, auditable process for granting, reviewing, and revoking access.
SLOs: initial decision within 2 business days for standard requests; expedited same-day for critical production emergency access.

Step-by-step: 
1. Requestor submits "Access Request" form in company service portal. Required fields: system, role, justification, duration (if temporary), data sensitivity classification.
2. Automated pre-checks: portal validates requestor's manager, current last access review date, and whether request is for privileged tooling.
3. Manager approval: manager verifies business justification and duration.
4. Security review (if sensitive or privileged): security annotates required controls (MFA, IP restrictions, log forwarding) and approves or requests mitigations.
5. IT ops executes access change and documents ticket with audit evidence (user added, policy applied).
6. Scheduled re-certification: all temporary elevated accesses auto-expire; permanent roles appear on quarterly access review reports.

Revocation policy:
- Immediate revocation for terminated employees or contractors (HR/IT automation).
- For inactive accounts > 90 days, access is automatically disabled pending owner review.

Access Request template (example YAML snippet to paste into a ticket):
---
request_type: access
requestor: maya.patel@redwood.ai
system: model-inference-console
role_requested: inference-operator
justification: Debugging production latency spikes during rollout
duration_days: 14
data_classification: internal
approvals_required: [manager, security]
attachments: [runbook-link, incident-id]
---

3) Change Management (service & infra changes):
Purpose: Ensure changes are planned, communicated, and reversible while minimizing production impact.
Change categories and approvals:
- Standard: pre-approved, low-risk operational changes (e.g., routine backup config tweak). Notified via changelog.
- Normal: scheduled planned changes requiring CAB sign-off for changes > scheduled window or affecting >1 region.
- Emergency: unplanned changes to restore service. Post-facto review required.

Change process (normal):
1. Submit Change Request with: scope, rollback plan, impact analysis, execution window, monitoring plan, owner.
2. Risk assessment by SRE: categorize as low/medium/high. High requires legal/SEC review if data-bearing.
3. CAB review: for medium/high, present during weekly CAB meeting or urgent CAB if timeline short.
4. Approval: CAB decision recorded with explicit owners and fallbacks.
5. Execute during scheduled window; SRE monitors and records metrics (error rate, latency, token throughput).
6. Post-change review: publish brief change summary and lessons learned within 3 business days.

Emergency change playbook:
1. Declare emergency in the incident channel.
2. Authorize a single emergency owner (normally SRE on-call).
3. Execute rollback-first strategy where possible; capture all actions for post-facto review.
4. Within 48 hours, produce a Change Review document linking to incident postmortem.

4) Data Management Requirements:
- Data classification: public / internal / restricted / regulated. All vendor contracts must include data classification mapping and handling clauses.
- Minimum controls for restricted data: encrypted-at-rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, customer-managed keys (if required), access logs retained 365 days.
- Data retention and deletion: owners must document retention periods in the request; automated deletion or archival workflows must be in place for regulated datasets.

Data checklist for vendor onboarding:
- Does vendor process restricted or regulated data? (Y/N)
- Can the vendor sign required BAA / DPA? (Y/N)
- Encryption and key management options documented.
- Location of data centers and EU-residency alignment noted.

5) Procurement & Expenses:
Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- Up to $5k: Manager sign-off.
- $5k - $50k: Manager + Finance approval; Procurement looped for vendor setup.
- > $50k: Manager + Finance + Legal + Procurement + Security (if data handled).

Contracting steps (request to contract):
1. Requestor files Procurement Request with business case, estimated TCO, preferred vendor, and draft SOW (if applicable).
2. Finance verifies budget and cost center.
3. Procurement evaluates vendor, requests commercial terms, and runs economical comparisons.
4. Legal negotiates terms; execute MSA/PO.
5. Finance issues PO and creates cost coding.
6. Vendor setup: Procurement creates vendor record, tax/ACH info, and ensures onboarding documents are stored in the contract index.

Expense policy highlights:
- All travel must be pre-approved via Travel Pre-Approval form for reimbursement eligibility.
- Per diem rules: domestic $75/day, international variable by region (see Travel appendix).
- Card usage: corporate card holders may transact up to $10k per month per card; above that requires pre-approval from Finance.

Procurement request JSON example (paste into portal):
{
  "request_type": "procurement",
  "requestor": "liam.chen@redwood.ai",
  "vendor": "Acme-ModelOps",
  "estimated_annual_cost": "42000",
  "business_case": "Managed model monitoring integration for inference quality alerts",
  "approvals_required": ["manager","finance","procurement"]
}

6) Vendor Management Lifecycle:
Stages: request -> security & risk review -> commercial negotiations -> onboarding -> quarterly review -> renewal/exit.

Security & risk gating:
- Initial vendor questionnaire (standard 40-question assessment) for any vendor with production access or data handling.
- For vendors processing regulated data, require SOC2 Type II or equivalent and a dedicated security review.
- Pilot engagements limited to 3 months by default unless otherwise approved.

Vendor onboarding checklist (required artifacts):
- Signed MSA or PO
- Vendor contact and escalation matrix
- Security questionnaire completed and approved
- Data processing addendum (if required)
- Payment and tax forms on file
- Assigned Redwood vendor owner

Quarterly vendor review:
- Vendor owner completes a short quarterly health check: uptime SLA conformance, incidents in period, cost vs. value memo, renewal recommendation.

7) Travel & Expense Guidance:
Pre-approval required for any travel outside your home region or for travel where cost > $750.
Travel booking guidance:
- Use the corporate travel portal for flights and hotels where available.
- Economy for flights under 8 hours; premium economy / business for flights > 8 hours when approved.
- Hotels: select one-star-tier above the venue minimum for safety and proximity.
Expense submission: attach receipts, conference agenda, and pre-approval ID. Submit within 14 days of trip completion.

Noncompliance and recovery:
- Expenses submitted without pre-approval may be denied or routed for manager remediation with potential payroll offsets if non-reimbursable.

8) Templates & Forms (attached here as examples to copy):
- Access Request (fields: requestor, system, role, justification, duration, approvers)
- Procurement Request (fields: requestor, vendor, TCO, contract term, approvals)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (link to central questionnaire)
- Travel Pre-Approval (fields: traveler, purpose, budget code, estimated cost, manager approval)

9) Audit, Reporting & Metrics:
- Monthly procurement spend report by cost center and vendor owner.
- Quarterly access review results with remediation counts (goal: <=5 exceptions per quarter).
- Vendor risk dashboard: number of vendors processing regulated data, pending questionnaires, and high-risk escalations.

10) Escalation & Exceptions:
- If approvals exceed SLA (2 business days for access, 5 business days for procurement < $50k), the requestor may ping the appropriate approver and escalate to the owner team lead.
- Exceptions to policy must be documented with a temporary exception request and retained in the contract index. Exceptions expire within 90 days unless renewed.

Appendix A — Example RACI table (ascii):
Role             | Requestor | Manager | Finance | Procurement | Legal | Security | IT/Ops
-----------------|-----------|---------|---------|-------------|-------|----------|--------
Access (standard)| R         | A       | I       | I           | I     | C        | R      
Procure <$5k     | R         | A       | C       | I           | I     | I        | I      
Contract >$50k   | R         | C       | C       | C           | A     | A        | I      

Appendix B — Sample evidence checklist for audits:
- Access tickets with approval chain and timestamps.
- Signed MSAs or PO attachments in contract index.
- Vendor security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence if applicable.
- Travel pre-approval forms and receipts.
- Change requests with risk assessment and post-change notes.

Ownership & maintenance:
- Document owner: Finance-legal Ops (Maya Patel).
- Review cadence: annual policy review (owner initiates in Q4) or sooner when regulatory change occurs.
- Change log: record substantive updates in the portal changelog with links to versioned artifacts.

Related resources and links:
- Contract index (internal link)
- Security questionnaire (internal link)
- Finance portal / expense submission
- IT service portal (access requests)

Contact for questions:
- policy-questions@redwood.ai (for interpretations)
- procurement@redwood.ai (vendor & procurement questions)
- security@redwood.ai (access and vendor security)

End of playbook.
